text:
Joel Hofer has been the Blues' reason for hope this fall. He has started 15 games, is 8-6-1, and has saved 8.4 goals more than the shots he faced usually allow (goals saved above expected, or GSAx), in the 83rd percentile among goalies. His last five starts alone are worth +5.4.

The signature night came on Nov. 12 in Utah: 29 saves in a 1-0 win decided in an eight-round shootout, the kind of game a goalie wins by himself.

The details hold up. He is stopping 98.9% of low-danger shots against a league 96.3%, so the soft ones are not getting through, and he is .730 on high-danger chances against a league .685. Only 8.7% of his saves lead to another shot within three seconds, better rebound control than average.

This is not a hot start out of nowhere. He was +11.0 by our numbers last season in 46 games, and Evolving-Hockey had him at +24.5. The Athletic has already started looking at comparables for his next contract, which tells you how the conversation around him has changed.
